clips.title: The truth about Trump’s Truths
clips.description: As a POLITICO Journalism Institute trainee on the breaking news desk, I developed this analysis of U.S. President Donald Trump's Truth Social posts. POLITICO reporter Greg Svirnovskiy and I personally read and categorized 844 of Trump's posts twice each. I conducted all data analysis for the final story, and also developed the associated charts in Datawrapper. My work was featured on POLITICO's homepage, BlueSky feed, in a push notification to subscribers, and as the headline story of the June 5, 2026 edition of West Wing Playbook.

clips.title: Oberlin College Invested $1.2 Million in Israeli Companies in 2021, Investigation Finds
clips.description: After 20 years of student calls for endowment transparency, my reporting identified more than $52 million of Oberlin's foreign investments for the first time, drawing on previously unreported documents I uncovered in a public IRS database. My research involved hundreds of pages of records from the IRS, SEC, and national business registries around the world.

clips.title: Why Political Text Blasts Targeting College Students Are Drawing Outrage
clips.description: This story gave me a chance to report on the 2024 general election from an unusual local angle. At public universities, students' phone numbers are considered government records, making them accessible to FOIA. After the Harris campaign used this loophole to mass text students at Arizona State, triggering outrage from the University's Young Republicans, I FOIAed the FOIA logs at universities across the country to identify the companies acquiring and selling student numbers to advertisers and political campaigns.

clips.title: Trump Administration Financial Ethics Disclosures
clips.description: As a contractor for ProPublica's news applications teams, I developed automated scripts to populate and send public records requests at scale. Using Python and Zapier, I filed 193 OGE form 201 requests across 123 federal agencies, contributing more than 3,000 new financial ethics disclosures to ProPublica’s public database. (The new batch of documents is set to go live in late October, following an application redesign by ProPublica's team.)

clips.title: The Colleges that Shape Congress
clips.description: As an intern for the Chronicle of Higher Ed, I had the rare chance to shepherd this piece from pitch to publication. I scraped data from the Congressional Bioguide, parsed it using Python and regular expressions, and analyzed the data in R. I developed the data visualizations in Flourish and built the accompanying scrollytelling page using HTML, CSS, and jQuery. Doing so taught me a great deal about the production workflow of a large newsroom – as I consulted closely with news editors, web developers, and the data team to move the piece forward.

clips.title: Federal Inmate Complaints
clips.description: As a volunteer for the Data Liberation Project, I cleaned and analyzed records detailing 1,783,999 complaints of alleged mistreatment filed by federal prison inmates between 2000 and 2024. My work was subsequently cited as the primary data source for an investigative story published by NPR and The Marshall Project.

clips.title: Flaw in Campus Directory Exposes ID Numbers of Students, Staff, Faculty, Alumni
clips.description: For months, Reed College computer science students had begged college IT to fix serious security flaws in the campus database that would have allowed those in the know to impersonate anyone, from stealing another student's meal swipes to opening locked doors as the director of campus safety. Their concerns had been ignored, and – we later learned – their fixes dismissed for being too expensive. Following our reporting, the vulnerabilities were fixed within days.

clips.title: Common Data Set Engine
clips.description: Common Data Sets can be an invaluable source for higher ed reporters, who rely on them for standardized statistics when other sources remain delayed or incomplete. Yet they remain locked in poorly formatted PDFs scattered across individual university websites. This search engine - developed during my internship at The Hechinger Report – provides access to 4,690 Common Data Sets processed using automated search and OCR.

clips.title: At U. of Wisconsin, Underrepresented Students of Color Were Half as Likely to Be Accepted This Year
clips.description: This story began with a Slack message from my editor with an attached CSV and a request to surface anything interesting. My analysis of the data identified not only significant disparities in admission rates by race/ethnicity, but wild swings in those rates following the Supreme Court's 2023 decision to outlaw affirmative action. While it is common for institutions to release the demographic details of their enrolled class, to this day I am not aware of any other cases of an institution releasing racial data on the admissions process itself.
